newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares leap after coalition seeks polls.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares leap after coalition seeks polls.

text.p: Turkish shares jumped 4.5 percent on Monday morning in the wake of the Islamist-led government's call for early elections, shrugging off concern about further political uncertainty, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 index ended the morning session up 4.51 percent, or 72 points, at 1,667. It jumped 8.7 percent last week mainly on hopes of an alternative alliance to replace the crumbling coalition under Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
The prospect of a fresh government alliance outweighed the potentially unsettling impact of elections, brokers said. The banking sector posted the strongest gains, rising over seven percent.
"I think the market is still buying on expectations of an alternative government because there is no other solid development to boost the shares," said Tolga Ozkan Okay from Evis Securities.
Trading volume eased to 14.88 trillion lira ($105 million) from Friday's 15.93 trillion ($113 million).

The government's conservative coalition partners said on Monday early elections would be held this year under a deal between Erbakan and his deputy Tansu Ciller to ease pressure from the generals to carry out an anti-Islamist crackdown.

Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist leader, announced on Sunday he would step down in favour of True Path leader Tansu Ciller within a month. He said Foreign Minister Ciller would then head a caretaker government to go to elections, but set no date.
"The market does not believe that parliament approval for early polls this year can be secured because the legal procedures cannot be completed in time," said Hasan Soydan from Garanti Securities.
Under Turkish law parliament must set the date for elections with a majority vote. The coalition has 275 seats in the 550-member parliament, with two seats vacant.
Analysts say a group of True Path deputies may vote against early polls after only two years in office on fears they may not be reelected.
The inability to pass an election law might give the secularist opposition the chance to set up a new coalition.

Some brokers said the possibility of a caretaker leader from outside the existing alliance, such as main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz of the conservative Motherland Party, supported the strong early rally.
A benign technical scenario reinforced the uptrend, which came on the heels of a 4.3 percent gain on Friday, but brokers said there was strong index resistance above 1,700 points.
"There is resistance at 1,750 points. The volume of trading is good and it could continue to this level. But at that point selling could emerge," said Seyfullah Esen of Gedik Securities.
Expectation of a Treasury auction supported the bond market, where yields fell by around half a percentage point to 102 percent.
In the currency market, the strong demand for dollars seen last week faded. The Turkish lira fell to 141,510 against the dollar from 140,410 at Friday's close.
